rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline by testing a simple RNA-only model with PCA encoding. This clarifies the performance of a single modality and isolates the effect of the RNA encoder and profile setting, providing a reference point for comparing more complex configurations later.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting. It balances exploration by extending the rna_only model to multiprofile, which could reveal if leveraging multiple profiles improves performance. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly addresses a key design choice with minimal changes, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) with RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while maintaining multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (the successful combination from config_002) improves accuracy. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, a critical design choice, and builds on the promising multiprofile foundation.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.650124). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and scvi_n200) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, which is critical for model design, and builds on the strongest current baseline without introducing other variables.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile settings and transformer aggregation (config_006: 0.6529 accuracy) outperform others. This experiment tests using the scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation (config_009), isolating the effect of the RNA encoder while maintaining the effective aggregation method. It balances exploration (testing a new RNA encoder) and exploitation (building on successful aggregation) to determine if scgpt improves accuracy further.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.652970). This experiment tests whether combining this RNA representation with image data (resnet50) using transformer aggregation and concat fusion can further improve performance, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploitation of the current top RNA model with exploration of multimodal benefits.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA and resnet50 image encoders (e.g., config_032) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6878). This experiment tests whether switching from transformer aggregation and concat fusion (used in config_032) to avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion could improve performance. It isolates the impact of aggregation and fusion methods, which are critical design choices, while keeping RNA and image encoders consistent. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of alternative fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50 achieve the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests using scvi_n200 with a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and weighted fusion, which could improve performance. It isolates the effect of the image encoder while maintaining the effective fusion strategy from the current best, balancing exploration of image encoder quality and exploitation of proven fusion methods.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether using scgpt RNA encoder instead of scvi_n200 in the same multimodal setup could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choice while keeping other components consistent, directly addressing a key design choice with high potential to yield insights under the remaining budget.

Existing evidence shows config_039 (multimodal, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests config_050 (multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat), which uses a different RNA encoder (scgpt) but shares the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion type as config_039. This isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice, which could reveal if scgpt outperforms scvi_n200 in this setup. Since the budget is exhausted, this comparison is critical to validate whether the current best's RNA encoder is optimal.
